2607.02175.title: A rubric-based controlled comparison of frontier language models on expert-authored clinical reasoning tasks
2607.02175.paper_summary: Multiple-choice medical benchmarks are increasingly saturated, and recent rubric-based evaluations such as HealthBench have shown that open-ended clinical performance is far from solved - its "Hard" subset top score remains 32%. We present a small, deliberately difficult evaluation dataset of five clinician-authored clinical scenarios spanning four specialties (anaesthesia, internal/family medicine, emergency medicine, and obstetrics), each accompanied by an atomic, weighted, MECE rubric (25-62 criteria per task; 184 criteria total) authored from a clinician-drafted golden answer. We evaluate three frontier models: GPT 5.4, Claude Opus 4.7, and Gemini 3.1 Pro. Mean rubric pass rates were 0.47 (Claude), 0.39 (GPT), and 0.37 (Gemini). The central finding is an inversion of clinical priority: the highest-weighted (weight-5, critical) criteria passed at only 32.4-41.7%, while low-stakes weight-1 criteria passed at 80-90%. 56 of 108 critical (weight-5) criteria (52%) were satisfied by no model. Three LLM autoraters reproduced expert met/not-met labels on 92.8-94.7% of 552 graded criteria. We position this as a methods-and-preliminary-findings contribution: the five tasks demonstrate a scalable, defensible pipeline ready to develop into a large-scale benchmark.
2607.02175.paper_summary_zh: 多選醫療基準正日益飽和，最近基於評分標準的評估如 HealthBench 顯示，開放式臨床表現遠未解決 - 其「困難」子集的最高分仍然是 32%。我們提出了一個小型、故意困難的評估數據集，包含五個臨床醫生撰寫的臨床情境，涵蓋四個專科（麻醉學、內科/家庭醫學、急診醫學和婦產科），每個情境都附有一個原子化、加權的 MECE 評分標準（每個任務 25-62 條標準；總共 184 條標準），這些標準是根據臨床醫生撰寫的金標準答案編寫的。我們評估了三個前沿模型：GPT 5.4、Claude Opus 4.7 和 Gemini 3.1 Pro。平均評分通過率為 0.47（Claude）、0.39（GPT）和 0.37（Gemini）。中心發現是臨床優先級的反轉：權重最高的（權重-5，關鍵）標準的通過率僅為 32.4-41.7%，而低風險的權重-1 標準的通過率則為 80-90%。108 個關鍵（權重-5）標準中有 56 個（52%）未被任何模型滿足。三個 LLM 自動評分者在 552 條評分標準上重現了專家的符合/不符合標籤，準確率為 92.8-94.7%。我們將此定位為方法與初步發現的貢獻：這五個任務展示了一個可擴展、可辯護的管道，準備發展成為一個大規模基準。
